registered_before: any real-data codebook, reference, baseline or attacker fit of this study (committed before ENGINEERING_LOCK)
status: predictions, not gates; never revised after outcome-bearing runs

predictions.question: Does at least one compact (finite-code, m >= 2) policy meet the full inner score contract (accuracy, true-label log loss within 0.01 nats, Brier within 0.005, gain retention, gain >= 0.03) on every seed?
predictions.reasoning: U-teacher codes preserve U's decisions exactly; with m = 8 cells per predicted class the mean KL to the teacher should be small, but occupation's six-class confidence is finely spread and its true-label log loss may move by more than 0.01; RAW-J-teacher codes start ~0.013 nats worse than U on occupation log loss and are likely ineligible

predictions.question: Does a privacy-trained policy (LOCAL, SEQ-12, SEQ-21 or JOINT) beat task-only compression (T*) by more than 0.02 pair AUC (assessment point estimate) while eligible?
predictions.reasoning: the decisions themselves carry most of the score-only SEX signal (decision-only pair AUC ~0.69-0.74 in the source tables); confidence coarsening can remove only the remainder, and the log-loss allowance limits it

predictions.question: Does JOINT beat BOTH sequential orders at matched teacher/rate on mean inner pair AUC (any margin)?
predictions.reasoning: JOINT's fitting objective dominates its witnesses by construction, but held-out recovery is noisy and plug-in MI on sparse pair tables is optimistic

predictions.question: Is the strongest control (T* / C_global) a simple compression (task-only family or class-only) rather than a continuous source or official reference?
predictions.reasoning: continuous sources include composed code readers and cannot be stronger than their codes; FARE/LEACE references were task-infeasible under the earlier accuracy gates and the new log-loss/Brier gates are stricter
